proposals.before: Guang's great-great-grandfather Zhongxiang was a general at the beginning of the Han, campaigned against rebel Qiang at Suchang—Suchang is Didao—and, outnumbered, died there.
proposals.after: Guang's great-grandfather Zhongxiang was a general at the beginning of the Han, campaigned against rebel Qiang at Suchang—Suchang is Didao—and, outnumbered, died there.
proposals.reason: 曾祖 is great-grandfather, not great-great-grandfather.

proposals.before: Zhongxiang's son Bokao came for the mourning and therefore was buried east of the river at Didao; thereupon the family settled there and for generations were a great clan of the western provinces.
proposals.after: Zhongxiang's son Bokao came for the mourning and therefore buried him east of the river at Didao; thereupon the family settled there and for generations were a great clan of the western provinces.
proposals.reason: The buried person is Zhongxiang; 葬 is not Bokao's own burial.

proposals.before: His grandfather Yan was General Who Guards the Marches under Zhang Gui and village marquis of Anshi.
proposals.after: His grandfather Yan was General of Martial Guards under Zhang Gui and village marquis of Anshi.
proposals.reason: 武衛將軍 is the Martial Guard generalship, not a march-guarding title.

proposals.before: Near Lu Guang's fall, Duan Ye of Jingzhao declared himself governor of Liang and named Meng Min of Zhao prefect of Dunhuang and Sha province, with Li Xuansheng as magistrate of Xiaogu.
proposals.after: Near Lu Guang's fall, Duan Ye of Jingzhao declared himself governor of Liang and, taking Dunhuang prefect Meng Min of Zhao commandery as inspector of Sha province, assigned Xuansheng magistrate of Xiaogu.
proposals.reason: Meng Min is already Dunhuang prefect and is appointed 沙州刺史; Xiaogu is a separate assignment for Xuansheng.

proposals.before: When Meng Min died soon after, Dunhuang protector Guo Qian and administrator Suo Xian, finding Li Xuansheng gentle, firm, and a just magistrate, raised him to General Who Pacifies the Shakes and prefect of Dunhuang.
proposals.after: When Meng Min died soon after, Dunhuang protector Guo Qian and administrator Suo Xian, finding Li Xuansheng gentle, firm, and a just magistrate, raised him to General Who Pacifies the North and prefect of Dunhuang.
proposals.reason: 甯朔 is Ningshuo (pacify the north), not Shakes.

proposals.before: When Ye usurped the title king of Liang, his guard general Suo Si slandered Xuansheng to Ye; Ye therefore appointed Suo Si prefect of Dunhuang, led five hundred horsemen westward, and, still twenty li short, sent Xuansheng a message ordering him to yield to himself.
proposals.after: When Ye usurped the title king of Liang, his guard general Suo Si slandered Xuansheng to Ye; Ye therefore appointed Suo Si prefect of Dunhuang; Si led five hundred horsemen westward and, still twenty li short, sent Xuansheng a message ordering him to yield.
proposals.reason: 率騎五百而西 has Suo Si, not Ye, as subject.

proposals.before: In the fourth year of Long'an, Then Tang Yao of Jinchang sent a call across six commanderies, raising Li Xuansheng to grand commander, grand general, Duke of Liang, governor of Qin and Liang, and colonel of the Qiang.
proposals.after: In the fourth year of Long'an, Tang Yao, grand administrator of Jinchang, sent a call across six commanderies, raising Li Xuansheng to grand commander, grand general, Duke of Liang, governor of Qin and Liang, and colonel of the Qiang.
proposals.reason: The word Then is an untranslated leftover, and Tang Yao's office 晉昌太守 is reduced to of Jinchang.

proposals.before: In the fourth year of Long'an, Then prefect of Jinchang Tang Yao circulated a proclamation through six commanderies and recommended Xuansheng as grand commander-in-chief, grand general, duke of Liang, concurrently shepherd of Qin and Liang two provinces, and colonel who protects the Qiang.
proposals.after: In the fourth year of Long'an, the prefect of Jinchang Tang Yao circulated a proclamation through six commanderies and recommended Xuansheng as grand commander-in-chief, grand general, duke of Liang, concurrently shepherd of Qin and Liang two provinces, and colonel who protects the Qiang.
proposals.reason: Then before prefect is not in the Chinese and breaks the English.

proposals.before: He proclaimed an amnesty, adopted the Gengzi era name, and posthumously titled his grandfather Yan Prince Jing of Liang and his father Chang Prince Jian of Liang.
proposals.after: He proclaimed an amnesty, adopted the Gengzi era name, and posthumously titled his grandfather Yan Duke Jing of Liang and his father Chang Duke Jian of Liang.
proposals.reason: 公 is duke, not prince; the literal already has duke.

proposals.before: He appointed Tang Yao General Who Punishes the East, Guo Qian libationer of military counsel, Suo Xian left chief clerk, Zhang Miao right chief clerk, Yin Jianxing left marshal, Zhang Tishun right marshal, Zhang Tiao left chief clerk of the shepherd's office, Linghu Yi right chief clerk, Zhang Lin senior recorder of the grand treasury, Song Yao and Zhang Su as retainers—Yao added General Who Smashes the Charge, Su added General Who Rouses Might—Suo Chengming right marshal of the shepherd's office, Linghu Qian General Who Guards the Marches and prefect of Jinxing, Fan Deyu General Who Pacifies the Distance and prefect of Xijun, Zhang Jing General Who Smashes the Charge and prefect of Hehuang, Suo Xun General Who Rouses the Distance and prefect of Xiping, Zhao Kai escort of piebald horses and prefect of Daxia, Suo Ci General Who Displays Might, Yin Liang prefect of Xi'an, Linghu He prefect of Wuwei, Suo Shu prefect of Wuxing, in order to summon and comfort the eastern summer.
proposals.after: He appointed Tang Yao General Who Punishes the East, Guo Qian libationer of military counsel, Suo Xian left chief clerk, Zhang Miao right chief clerk, Yin Jianxing left marshal, Zhang Tishun right marshal, Zhang Tiao left chief clerk of the shepherd's office, Linghu Yi right chief clerk, Zhang Lin senior recorder of the grand treasury, Song Yao and Zhang Su as retainers—Yao added General Who Smashes the Charge, Su added General Who Rouses Might—Suo Chengming right marshal of the shepherd's office, Linghu Qian General Who Guards the Marches and prefect of Jinxing, Fan Deyu General Who Pacifies the Distance and prefect of Xijun, Zhang Jing General Who Smashes the Charge and prefect of Hehuang, Suo Xun General Who Rouses the Distance and prefect of Xiping, Zhao Kai escort of piebald horses and prefect of Daxia, Suo Ci prefect of Guangwu, Yin Liang prefect of Xi'an, Linghu He prefect of Wuwei, Suo Shu prefect of Wuxing, in order to summon and comfort the eastern Xia.
proposals.reason: The Chinese makes Suo Ci 廣武太守 only; General Who Displays Might is invented, Guangwu is dropped, and 東夏 is not the season summer.

proposals.before: Humbly I reflect: Your Majesty's way matches Shao Kang; your virtue equals Guang Wu; you continue Heaven's line and stand in the succession; your will is to clear the letter summer.
proposals.after: Humbly I reflect: Your Majesty's way matches Shao Kang; your virtue equals Guang Wu; you continue Heaven's line and stand in the succession; your will is to clear the heartland Xia.
proposals.reason: 函夏 is the contained Xia / heartland, not letter summer.

proposals.before: Duke Huan of Qi marched when lords withheld duty; Duke Wen of Jin struck Chengpu and so lit his name at Ji'tu and raised the work of uniting the realm—the nine provinces rode on his design, and the Spring and Autumn Annals excused his acting without orders.
proposals.after: When Duke Huan of Qi raised the army at Shaoling, the lords were disrespectful; when Duke Wen of Jin launched the campaign at Chengpu, he made merit shine at Jiantu and raised the work of a single hegemon—the nine regions relied on his great plan, and the Spring and Autumn Annals excused his acting without orders.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic omits Shaoling and misrenders 踐土 as Ji'tu.

proposals.before: Li Xuansheng told his council, "When the Hexi broke apart and heroes contended, they had chosen him, though he lacked virtue, and that he had not slept for thinking of the people.
proposals.after: Li Xuansheng told his council, "When the Hexi broke apart and heroes contended, I, though lacking virtue, was put forward by the worthies, and I have not forgotten sleep and food while thinking how to save the people.
proposals.reason: The Chinese speech is first-person (吾); the idiomatic rendering switches to third-person him and drops the sleep-and-food clause.

proposals.before: East of Zhangye the Jin survivors, though under barbarian rule, long for your grace more keenly than the Shang once longed for the lord of the west.
proposals.after: East of Zhangye the Jin survivors, though under barbarian rule, long for righteous rule more keenly than the Shang once longed for the lord of the west.
proposals.reason: Xiangyi sifeng is longing for righteousness and civilizing influence, not your grace addressed to the council.

proposals.before: When he first marched west he left his daughter Jing'ai in the care of her grandfather Yin Wen.
proposals.after: When he first marched west he left his daughter Jing'ai in the care of her maternal grandfather Yin Wen.
proposals.reason: Wai zu is specifically the maternal grandfather, which the literal already preserves.

proposals.before: Dunhuang is thickly peopled, rules the Western Regions for ten thousand li, and is the root of army and state; I name my second son Rang General Who Pacifies the Shakes, colonel of the western Yi, and Dunhuang prefect to bind the western marches and quiet distant lands.
proposals.after: Dunhuang is thickly peopled, rules the Western Regions for ten thousand li, and is the root of army and state; I name my second son Rang General Who Pacifies the North, colonel of the western Yi, and Dunhuang prefect to bind the western marches and quiet distant lands.
proposals.reason: 甯朔將軍 is Ningshuo, General Who Pacifies the North; 'Shakes' is a corruption of 朔, not a people or office.

proposals.before: Moreover Dunhuang commandery's population is great and prosperous; it controls the western regions and governs ten thousand li; it is root of army and state; rashly he appoints his second son Rang as General Who Pacifies the Shakes, colonel of the western Yi, Dunhuang prefect, to gather and govern Kun's descendants and pacify the different quarters.
proposals.after: Moreover Dunhuang commandery's population is great and prosperous; it controls the western regions and governs ten thousand li; it is root of army and state; he thereupon appoints his second son Rang as General Who Pacifies the North, colonel of the western Yi, Dunhuang prefect, to gather and govern the descendant peoples and pacify the different quarters.
proposals.reason: 輒 means thereupon, not rashly; 甯朔 is Ningshuo, not Shakes; 昆裔 is descendant lineages, not 'Kun's descendants'.

proposals.before: Moreover your subject's province's borders wind far; fierce bandits are not yet removed; he ought to follow the deputy commander for mobile and stationary disposition; rashly he appoints his heir Shiye to supervise forward armies' military affairs, General Who Comforts the Army, colonel who protects the Qiang, to command and seize the forward army and go as your subject's vanguard.
proposals.after: Moreover your subject's province's borders wind far; fierce bandits are not yet removed; he ought to follow the deputy commander for mobile and stationary disposition; he thereupon appoints his heir Shiye to supervise forward armies' military affairs, General Who Comforts the Army, colonel who protects the Qiang, to command and seize the forward army and go as your subject's vanguard.
proposals.reason: 輒 here is sequential 'then/thereupon', not 'rashly'.

proposals.before: Read Zhuge Liang's warnings and Ying Qu's frank memorials from start to finish; the way of the sages is all there.
proposals.after: Read Zhuge Liang's warnings and Ying Qu's frank memorials from start to finish; the teaching of Zhou and Kong is all there.
proposals.reason: 周孔之教 names Zhou and Kong; 'the sages' drops those referents.

proposals.before: The Zhang kings fell from cliff; the Liang queen dropped into gorge; pure wind in distant wastes was lost forever; girdle-pendants sank together and overturned in drowning.
proposals.after: The Zhang kings fell from cliff; the Liang house dropped into the gorge; pure wind in distant wastes was lost forever; girdle-pendants sank together and overturned in drowning.
proposals.reason: 梁後 is parallel to 張王 as a ruling house (the Liang/Later Liang line), not a queen.

proposals.before: The Lu house bred strife in the inner chambers and saw its rafters crash;
proposals.after: The Lü house bred strife in the inner chambers and saw its rafters crash;
proposals.reason: 呂 is the Lü clan of Later Liang, not the Lu house.

proposals.before: When Shiye heard it, he led troops back and was pressed by Xun.
proposals.after: When Shiye heard it, he led troops back and was pressed by Mengxun.
proposals.reason: 遜 here abbreviates 蒙遜 (Mengxun), not a separate person Xun.

proposals.before: Your subject has heard that Heaven's son loves mankind afterward—earnest and utmost.
proposals.after: Your subject has heard that the Son of Heaven's love for the people is earnest and utmost.
proposals.reason: Literal 天之子愛人後 garbles 天子之愛人; 'afterward' is not the sense, which is the ruler's devoted care for the people.

proposals.before: Xuansheng was established in Emperor An's Longan fourth year; down to the Song Emperor Shao's extinction in Jingping first year, he held the west of the river altogether twenty-four years.
proposals.after: Xuansheng was established in Emperor An's Longan fourth year; down to extinction in the Song Emperor Shao's Jingping first year, the house held the west of the river altogether twenty-four years.
proposals.reason: 滅 and 據河右凡二十四年 describe the Western Liang house's span, not Li Gao's personal rule through 423.

decisions.reason: 索慈為廣武太守 only; the invented generalship drops Guangwu, and 東夏 is the eastern Xia, not the season summer.

decisions.reason: 志清函夏 is clearing the contained/heartland Xia, not a letter summer.

decisions.after: When Duke Huan of Qi raised the army at Shaoling, the lords withheld duty; Duke Wen of Jin struck Chengpu and so lit his name at Jiantu and raised the work of uniting the realm—the nine provinces rode on his design, and the Spring and Autumn Annals excused his acting without orders.
decisions.reason: The original omits 召陵 and misromanizes 踐土 as Ji'tu; the proposed rewrite also recasts 業隆一匡 and 九域賴其弘猷 without need.

decisions.reason: 向義思風 is turning toward righteousness and longing for civilizing influence, not your grace addressed to the council.
